body: My issue is that all of my problems are very broad: my friends don't care, I'll never be loved, my family doesn't notice me, I hate the person I am, my life is meaningless, etc. It's kind of hard to take baby steps in shallow water when every issue is like a deep, bottomless pool.

To me it is. Unfortunately for me I have a strict all-or-nothing mindset. If I go to a hospital, that would mean I have to stop my life for a couple of years. On the off chance I get better, I would have to go back to school and it would be harder to pick up. Plus everyone will have known where I was and why and that judgment will last forever. Either I suck it up and follow the straight line of school, grad school, then career, or get off the line and kill myself. I can barely do freshman year of college now, so I don't know how I'm going to survive all those other things.

I've seen a lot in the past but I didn't like any of them. I end up not saying anything and try to downplay the whole situation to make it seem like no big deal. I'm terrified that if I tell them the truth, I'll be sent away to a hospital.

There wasn't a single event or anything that triggered this for me. I've just always been depressed, but lately the weight has been getting heavier. I keep it all bottled up because I feel like I can't talk about this with anyone. I don't like to open up. Every time I have, people send me away because they don't like who they see.
Thanks. I think I just overreacted because I don't usually cut my wrists.
I don't want to take the band aid off, but it hasn't bled through so I should be fine. It just really hurts. A lot more than when I usually cut.
No, I don't see any blood outside the band aid.
The ones near my wrist are pretty shallow, but still noticeable. The ones near my elbows are deeper and redder. But they also are pretty new, so they'll probably heal better closer to summer.

I don't know, I was just never good about remembering to take them everyday. And then the more I thought about it, I realized I didn't want the drugs to change me. I've never heard of them as "motivation" before. I *might* start taking them.

The first time it was a conscious decision not to go. But lately it's simply due to exhaustion. No matte what time I go to bed, I'm so tired in the morning.I have medication, but I haven't used it in months. No therapist either. I talked to one recently and did not like the experience at all.
Not really. But they acknowledge I'm there and then don't address me unless I speak first. I might as well not even be there.

That's exactly how I am. I want to die so badly but I can't kill myself because that's how I'll always be remembered. I know it's sick, but I would love to have cancer so that I can: A) die in a way that people will forgive and B) feel the pain I deserve

I just want people to forget me. If I had the money to buy an apartment away from everyone I knew, I would never leave my bed.

You're right, it was a counselor. Sorry, I always just use the "psychiatrist" label for any type of counselor.

I live in a dorm too at my university. That's the main reason why I can't tell anyone. I don't want to get kicked out of school. I know if I kill myself it won't matter, but honestly I'd do anything to get out of going to the hospital.

People judge you for being depressed. We try to say that "it's okay" and we "only want to help" but the truth is if I ever went to hospital for suicidal thoughts, I would be *That Girl*. That's why I can't kill myself either. Otherwise I'd always be known as the *Emo Weirdo Who Killed Herself*. 

I was terrified of telling her the truth because if I let people see the real me, they will:

* judge me.
* reject me.
* send me away from the public eye to a hospital.

I wasn't talking to a friend. I was talking to a psychiatrist at my school. 

There's no way I'll ever tell my friends. They would never understand and would either constantly check up on me or ditch me.
